scheme_name: Award of Pre-Matric Scholarship to Other Economically Backward Class (OEBC) Students
description:
The Award of Pre-Matric Scholarship to Other Economically Backward Class (OEBC) Students is a significant welfare scheme initiated by the Government of India.

This scheme was launched in 2014 under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

It aims to provide financial assistance to students from Other Economically Backward Classes who are pursuing education at the pre-matriculation level.

The primary objective of this scholarship is to reduce the dropout rate among students belonging to economically weaker sections.

The scheme specifically targets students studying in classes 1 to 10.

The government has set a measurable target of supporting at least 1 million students annually through this scholarship.

The scholarship amount varies based on the class in which the student is enrolled.

For students in classes 1 to 5, the scholarship amount is ₹1,000 per annum.

For students in classes 6 to 8, the scholarship amount is ₹3,000 per annum.

For students in classes 9 and 10, the scholarship amount is ₹4,000 per annum.

This financial assistance is intended to cover educational expenses such as school fees, books, and other necessary materials.

The eligibility criteria for this scholarship are clearly defined.

Students must belong to the Other Economically Backward Classes as defined by the government.

The annual family income of the applicant must not exceed ₹1 lakh.

Students must be enrolled in recognized schools.

There are no specific educational qualifications required for eligibility as this scheme targets students from classes 1 to 10.

The application process for the scholarship is systematic and requires several steps.

Interested candidates must visit the official website of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

They need to fill out the application form available on the website.

The application form requires personal details such as name, age, class, and school information.

Applicants must also provide details regarding their family income.

A crucial part of the application is the submission of supporting documents.

These documents include an income certificate issued by a competent authority.

Students must also submit proof of their admission to a recognized school.

A caste certificate may be required to confirm the applicant's OEBC status.

Once the application is completed, it must be submitted to the respective state government or union territory.

Each state has its own designated authority for processing these applications.

The timeline for application submission typically aligns with the academic calendar.

Applications are usually invited at the beginning of the academic year.

The deadline for submission may vary by state but generally falls between June and July.

Disbursement of the scholarship amount is made directly to the bank account of the beneficiary.

The scholarship is disbursed on an annual basis.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

Each state government has a dedicated department that oversees the implementation of the scheme.

For example, in Maharashtra, the Social Justice and Special Assistance Department is responsible.

In Uttar Pradesh, the Department of Social Welfare manages the scholarship program.

The contact details for these departments can be found on their respective official websites.

The scholarship scheme has seen significant uptake since its inception.

As of 2023, over 1.5 million students have benefited from the scheme.

The government allocates a budget of approximately ₹500 crores annually for this scholarship.

This financial commitment underscores the government's dedication to supporting education for economically backward classes.

The scheme has been instrumental in improving enrollment rates in schools.

It has also contributed to reducing the dropout rates among students from economically weaker sections.

The scholarship is part of a broader initiative to promote education and uplift marginalized communities.

The government has also launched awareness campaigns to inform eligible students about the scholarship.

These campaigns are conducted through various media channels including social media, print, and community outreach programs.

The impact of the scholarship can be seen in the increased number of students completing their education.

The scheme has also encouraged parents to invest in their children's education.

The government regularly reviews the scheme to ensure its effectiveness and reach.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to make necessary improvements.

The scholarship is a vital component of the government's efforts to promote social equity.

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations.

The scheme is also part of the larger framework of welfare initiatives aimed at empowering disadvantaged groups.

In conclusion, the Award of Pre-Matric Scholarship to Other Economically Backward Class Students is a crucial program.

It provides essential financial support to students from economically weaker backgrounds.

The scholarship not only alleviates the financial burden on families but also promotes educational attainment.

With specific eligibility criteria and a straightforward application process, the scheme is accessible to many.

The government's commitment to funding and improving this initiative reflects its dedication to education and social justice.
